title: Angels Landing Walk
map_label: 3D view of Zion Canyon following the hiker along the Angels Landing trail

stops.alt: Angels Landing rising above the Virgin River from the lower trail
stops.title: The Grotto shuttle stop
stops.text: You start beside the Virgin River at {elev}. The fin you can see ahead is Angels Landing.

stops.commons_file: Angels Landing, Zion National Park, Utah (8096062363).jpg
stops.alt: Angels Landing seen from the switchbacks below
stops.title: Up the canyon wall
stops.text: Paved switchbacks climb the cliff face, with Angels Landing towering beside you.

winter.text: Paved switchbacks climb the cliff face. Snow and ice can make the trail slippery in winter. The photo, from the West Rim Trail, shows the same canyon under snow.

stops.alt: Paved trail through the narrow, shaded Refrigerator Canyon
stops.title: Refrigerator Canyon
stops.text: A shaded slot between sheer walls. It stays cool even in summer, and the trail goes nearly flat.

winter.text: A shaded slot between sheer walls where the trail goes nearly flat. The shade means ice can linger here after the sun has cleared the open parts of the trail.

stops.alt: Stone switchbacks of Walter's Wiggles seen from below
stops.title: Walter's Wiggles
stops.text: Twenty-one tight stone switchbacks stacked up the rock, the steepest part before Scout Lookout.

stops.commons_file: Towards Angel's Landing, Zion National Park, UT (8586599892).jpg
stops.alt: The narrow trail leading from Scout Lookout toward the Angels Landing fin
stops.title: Where most hikers stop
stops.text: The final half-mile follows a narrow fin with drops on both sides, and needs a permit.

winter.text: The final half-mile follows a narrow fin with drops on both sides, and needs a permit. Ice and snow make the chains section more dangerous, so check the park's current conditions first.

stops.alt: Hikers using chains along the sandstone ridge of Angels Landing
stops.title: Holding the chains
stops.text: Steel chains bolted into the sandstone guide you up the last stretch.

winter.text: Steel chains bolted into the sandstone guide you up the last stretch. In winter they can be icy, so check the park's current conditions before you go.

stops.alt: View down Zion Canyon from the summit of Angels Landing
stops.title: Angels Landing
stops.text: About {gain} above where you started, with Zion Canyon spread out below.

seasons.note: Season view is illustrative: snow and colour are drawn on the map, not measured. The photos are real.
